A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same preference-data selection work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching content across substantial renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original DPO experiments, including benchmark win rates, training dynamics, iterative training, and ablations.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original experiments, including retained benchmark results and additional Qwen evaluations and subset-size analyses.

M1.justification: BeeS retains DM-MUL's clipped-probability fusion rule for two sources. v3 generalizes aggregation to K external/implicit margin sources and removes the DM-ADD alternative, while retaining the seed-model scoring and ranked-subset selection pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same SFT corpus, TL;DR, HH, UltraFeedback, its Llama/Mistral variants, and AlpacaEval evaluations. Summarization, helpfulness/harmlessness, dialogue, and online preference-learning coverage remain unchanged; Qwen expands model configurations.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 3 adds alpha-DPO and beta-DPO alongside SimPO, while KTO and IPO disappear from that low-beta comparison previously presented in v1 Table 6. Random and Low-Gap are removed from the Mistral comparison, and DM-ADD results disappear throughout. The main random, IFD, single-margin, and full-data comparator families remain.

E3.justification: v3 adds Qwen-2.5-7B/14B configurations and subset-size sweeps covering 3k, 6k, 10k, 15k, and full-data training, including an explicitly beta=0.01 Instruct experiment. Existing evaluation sizes, metrics, and decoding temperature remain. Section 4.4 names Llama-UltraFeedback for the algorithm-transfer ablation, whereas Figure 4 names UltraFeedback, leaving that experiment's dataset assignment unresolved.

E4.justification: v3 adds systematic subset-size sensitivity studies, larger-model transfer tests, and a Skywork/ArmoRM margin-disagreement analysis on online-generated pairs. The explicit one-versus-two-epoch comparison and Mistral hyperlink case analysis disappear. Existing margin-distribution, training-dynamics, and small-beta failure analyses are substantially retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seed identifiers, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests for the benchmark results. No statistical testing procedure accompanies v3's new blue highlighting of degraded results.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes DM-MUL/BeeS win rates from 87.25 to 90.25 on HH and 90.68 to 91.68 on UltraFeedback. Table 2 changes UltraFeedback Llama-3-Instruct LC/WR from 28.30/28.39 to 30.03/30.46. v3 also adds Qwen and subset-size results and removes several result entries. Iterative-DPO values are retained from v1 Table 3 in v3 Figure 3.

T1.justification: The parameter-shrinkage and inflation reasoning is retained. v3 extends Equation 3 from two to K margin sources and explicitly states conditional independence. It also corrects the background DPO loss from negative sigmoid to negative log-sigmoid.

C1.justification: v3 presents general multi-source Bayesian aggregation as the methodological contribution and explicitly extends the advertised performance claim to Qwen. The central claims about margin-based selection, improved alignment using roughly 10% of the data, and applicability to iterative DPO remain.

C2.justification: v3 introduces a smaller-beta/data-efficiency explanation, explicitly qualifies the probability mapping as an approximation, and adds a limitation concerning evaluation only up to 14B parameters. It removes the Mistral hyperlink explanation and the explicit recommendation against small beta, while retaining the instability examples and mitigation advice.

D1.justification: v3 states the general DPO learning rate as 5e-7 and clarifies that implicit reward models need training only in the first online iteration. It removes v1's AdamW, cosine-schedule, batch-size-32, and explicit single-epoch online-training disclosures. Dataset statistics, evaluation prompts, clipping bounds, and hardware/time information are largely retained.

R1.justification: v3 expands related work to discuss competing views of difficult preference examples, citing RS-DPO, RIP, and Principled Data Selection for Alignment, alongside additional preference-elicitation and aggregation work. The positioning of data selection as complementary to DPO objective modifications remains.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: related work moves into the introduction, margin-distribution analysis moves into methodology, iterative experiments merge into Section 4.3, and appendices are reorganized. Method and experimental explanations are extensively rewritten, with DM renamed BeeS and TOP/MID/BOT renamed P/Z/N.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Tables and plots are extensively regrouped: iterative and architecture results become panels in Figures 3 and 4, training curves are consolidated in Figure 2, and DPO-variant bar charts are merged. New scatter and subset-size panels and revised table highlighting further change the presentation.

improvement.justification: The subset-size sweeps and Qwen evaluations better establish how data efficiency varies with training budget and model choice. The corrected DPO formula, explicit approximation caveat, and model-scale limitation also improve clarity. These gains are limited by removed implementation details and comparator results, plus the conflicting dataset descriptions for Figure 4's ablation.
